History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
25-year-old woman with 2-day history of progressively worsening constant burning pain just below the umbilicus, associated mild nausea, feeling hot/sweaty, pink-tinged urine and urinary frequency; empirically treated as possible urinary tract infection with trimethoprim and advised pregnancy test and safety-net follow-up.

History:
• Chief complaint: Lower abdominal (“tummy”) pain.  
• Onset & course: Began ~2 days ago; gradual onset, progressively worsening.  
• Location/character: Constant burning pain localized just below the umbilicus; tender to palpation. No radiation.  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: None specified. Pain noticeable but patient able to ambulate and perform activities.  
• Associated urinary symptoms:  
  – Increased urinary frequency.  
  – Pink-tinged urine noted; uncertain frank hematuria.  
  – No dysuria, no urgency, no suprapubic burning.  
• Gastrointestinal: Mild nausea, no vomiting. Bowels previously constipated last week (resolved); currently normal, no diarrhea.  
• Constitutional: Feels hot/sweaty; temperature not measured. No reported fever measurement.  
• ROS screening (pertinent negatives): No shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, chest pain, headaches, or visual changes.  
• Gynecologic/sexual:  
  – Sexually active with single partner; last intercourse 4 days ago.  
  – On etonogestrel implant (Implanon) inserted 1 year ago; no barrier contraception.  
  – Still menstruating; last menstrual period reported as “about three weeks ago… two weeks ago” (conflict noted).  
  – Last STI screen 6 months ago – normal.  
  – Pregnancy considered possible but patient thinks unlikely.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Surgical history: None.  
• Obstetric/gynecologic: Etonogestrel implant in situ.  
• Medications:  
  – Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  

Social History:
• Lives in shared house with two roommates.  
• Employment: Accountant.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Social use; “not more than normal.”  
• Illicit drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• No relevant family history reported.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed/not documented during teleconsultation.)

Investigations:
• None performed; clinician discussed need for further tests (unspecified) and pregnancy test, but none done at time of call.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Possible urinary tract infection vs other causes of lower abdominal pain (e.g., gastrointestinal, gynecologic, pregnancy-related).  
• Plan:  
  – Empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (route/strength not documented) sent electronically to patient’s pharmacy.  
  – Encourage increased oral fluids and cranberry juice.  
  – Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Advise urine and/or other laboratory tests if no improvement.  

Issue 2: Rule out pregnancy.  
• Plan:  
  – Obtain home urine pregnancy test as soon as possible; report results.  

Issue 3: Symptom monitoring / safety netting.  
• Plan:  
  – Return or seek urgent care if worsening abdominal pain, persistent or high fever, vomiting, or other concerning symptoms.  
  – Routine follow-up in a few days if symptoms not improving.

General plan items: None additional.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing clinically expected elements: Allergies, vital signs, full medication list/reconciliation, physical examination, laboratory/urine analysis results.  
• Internal conflicts: Last menstrual period stated as “three weeks ago” then “two weeks ago.”  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional minor conversational noise, but clinically usable.
